title: Kinetic slice orchestrator: tunable latency-throughput mediation for prefill/decode
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal:
Design and prototype a modular 'Kinetic Slice Orchestrator' that mediates prefill/decode work by splitting requests into small time-boxed slices (kinetic slices) and scheduling them with tunable latency/throughput knobs. The orchestrator should: 1) expose policies for latency buckets, tenant-weighted fairness, and opportunistic coalescing; 2) accept kernel-selection hints from the kernel probe layer (attention sparsity, kv-cache locality, quantization-friendly path) and prefer slice placements that maximize throughput while respecting latency SLOs; 3) provide telemetry hooks for per-slice cost, kernel choice, and end-to-end request latency to feed Optimize and Console dashboards.

Motivation:
Current prefill/decode arbitration is brittle under mixed workloads: long prefill-heavy tenant bursts starve short low-latency requests and kernel changes (e.g., different attention kernels) cause sudden latency spikes. Instead of monolithic phase splitting, Kinetic Slices allow incremental execution and better backpressure handling, making it easier to: - implement hedging/fast-paths for latency-sensitive slices; - opportunistically batch slices that have compatible kernel requirements; - demote bulk background slices to lower throughput tiers.

Success criteria (first prototype):
- Median tail improvement for 1k concurrent mixed-tenancy benchmark: 15-25% reduction in p50/p95 latency for short (<=32 token) decode requests.
- Scheduler must produce stable fairness metric (tenant credit variance < 5% over 30m load test).
- No single-tenant prefill should push other tenants above their p99 budget more than 2% of test runtime.
- End-to-end cost impact measured in test cluster: <= 5% additional GPU utilization vs baseline for same throughput when enabling opportunistic batching.

Design decisions made so far:
- Use timeboxed slices (default 8ms wall clock) vs token-count slicing to allow kernel-aware decisions and preemption. Rationale: wall-clock time better correlates with kernel runtimes across quant/attn variants.
- Tenant credit model: hybrid of decay-based credits (to avoid starvation) and soft guarantees for latency SLAs. Credits can be tuned per-customer via Dedicated policy.
- Kernel hint surface: kernel_probe will emit three cheap signals per request: attention_sparsity_hint (low/medium/high), kv_locality_hint (hot/cold), preferred_kernels (list). Orchestrator will prefer co-locating slices with compatible hints to avoid kernel switching overhead.
- Coalescing policy: only coalesce slices when estimated merge win (latency vs token-cost) is positive; configurable threshold.

Trade-offs considered and rationale:
- Timebox vs token-slice: timebox can interrupt attention-heavy kernels mid-op; we accept occasional preemption overhead in favor of latency predictability.
- Strong fairness vs latency SLOs: primary guardrails favor latency SLOs for latency-sensitive tenants; fairness applies to best-effort/backfill workloads.
- Kernel affinity increases throughput but can fragment GPU utilization; we add opportunistic fallback to demote to generic kernel if fragmentation exceeds threshold.

Prototype plan and milestones:
1) Week 1-2: Internal simulator (ENG/bench) that models kinetic slices, kernel switching overheads, and tenant credit flows. (Owner: Markus)
2) Week 2-4: Runtime changes: slice abstraction in worker loop, kernel_hint API, basic scheduler policy (latency buckets + decay credits). Instrumentation added: per-slice metrics, kernel switch counters. (Owner: Markus + Runtime Team)
3) Week 4-5: Integration test harness with mixed workloads (short chat, long prefill, embeddings) + A/B run on staging cluster. Collect p50/p95/p99 and cost metrics. (Owner: Performance team)
4) Week 6: Design review and iteration based on staging results; prepare rollout gating criteria and runbook for Dedicated customers.

Open questions / risks:
- How to quantify kernel-switch cost for fused attention kernels that have variable run durations? (Action: add microbenchmarks per-model in kernel_probe)
- Interaction with KV cache warmup: slicing may split cache-friendly prefill across slices causing repeated cache population. Need guardrail to keep contiguous prefill for same request within small window. (Action: implement kv_locality_hint enforcement)
- Estimating merge-win requires lightweight cost model; ensure model is cheap and robust under noise.

Telemetry and dashboards needed:
- Per-slice: duration_ms, kernel_used, tokens_processed, tenant_key, latency_bucket, coalesced_flag
- Per-request aggregate: total_prefill_ms, total_decode_ms, kernel_switch_count
- Fairness metric via tenant credit time-series and normalized latency delta

Rollout plan:
- Canary on a fraction of runtime nodes with feature flag kinetic_slices_v1; start with coalescing disabled and timebox conservative (12ms).
- Enable coalescing in controlled A/B after positive staging results.
- Expose Dedicated policy knobs (latency_bucket_thresholds, tenant_credit_params) in Console.

Longer term goals (post-prototype):
- Integrate with admission control to gate background bulk prefill queues.
- Provide ML-driven slice sizing recommendations for common workloads via Optimize.
- Expose tenant QoS tiers to customers for SLA-driven credit tuning.
